verdict.rationale: cubic documents an official MCP server, with a dedicated docs page confirmed by probe, that coding agents connect to. Through it they can read review findings and codebase context, request PR reviews, triage PR and codebase-scan issues, and manage subscriptions and seats. Setup is documented for Cursor, Claude Code, VS Code, Codex and Gemini CLI. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the MCP server working in practice.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect an agent via an official MCP server

citations.quote: Connect cubic's MCP server to your coding agent to read review findings and codebase context, request PR reviews, and triage PR or codebase scan issues.
cubic's MCP server lets your coding agent read review findings, look up codebase documentation, request PR reviews, triage PR or codebase scan issues
Install and connect cubic in Cursor, Claude Code, VS Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, or another coding tool.
You can now ask your coding agent to check your cubic subscription, manage team seats and roles, and purchase more seats without leaving your MCP client.
official MCP server documented at https://docs.cubic.dev/ide/mcp-server
